newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mobutu envoy expected in S.Africa - officials.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu envoy expected in S.Africa - officials.

text.p: Zairean government envoy Honore Ngbanda was expected in South Africa on Wednesday to deliver President Mobutu Sese Seko's response to an invitation to peace talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, officials said.
"Mr Ngbanda is expected in South Africa this afternoon and he has asked to meet...Deputy President (Thabo) Mbeki," said a South African foreign ministry official.
President Nelson Mandela's spokesman, Parks Mankahlana, said: "We expect that he is carrying a formal response from President Mobutu to President Mandela's invitation to peace talks in South Africa."

Ngbanda and Kabila agreed in talks with South African officials last week to a face-to-face meeting between Mobutu and the rebel leader, whose forces control half of Zaire and threaten to take the capital within weeks.
Mankahlana played down Kabila's statement after returning to Lubumbashi last week that he would meet Mobutu only to receive his resignation and usher him out of office.
"The public statements notwithstanding, every communication between us and the two sides is marked by their commitment to finding a peaceful solution for Zaire," he said.

Mbeki, who was due back from the United States on Wednesday, has handled arrangements for the first direct meeting between Mobutu and Kabila. In Washington, Mbeki said he expected talks to take place "soon".
Mankahlana said he expected the next issue would be a venue. Mandela proposed Cape Town, but Mobutu, recovering from surgery for prostate cancer, has said he was too ill to travel to South Africa.
"The South African government is not wedded to any venue as long as there is a meeting between the Zairean authorities and the rebels and that the talks are serious," he said.
